text.p: Slovakia's largest drug producer Slovakofarma a.s. on Wednesday said it expected an after-tax profit of around 500 million crowns in 1996, compared with a 481.2 million crown net profit in 1995.

Slovakofarma's financial director Helena Jandikova told Reuters that the company planned to pay a dividend of "around" 200 crowns per share from the earnings compared with 250 crowns from its 1995 result.
Jendikova said last year's overall sales were roughly 4.4 billion crowns, up from four billion crowns in 1995.
She said the company planned to release its full 1996 results and its outlook for this year in the first week of March.
The company has called an annual shareholders meeting for May 15.
Slovakofarma's is one of the fastest rising stocks on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE), up 462 crowns on Wednesday to 4,874. It has risen from the 3,600 crown level at the beginning of this month.
